name: Ask the world's data
owner: DataHub core datasets (World Bank, NOAA, NASA, US Federal Reserve and others)
description: Ask a question about the world's key datasets (economy, climate, energy, markets) and get a short data story with charts and sources.
headline: Ask the world's data.|Get the *story.*
intro: Type a question in plain English about the economy, climate, energy or markets. You'll get a short answer with charts, built from trusted public datasets, with every source one click away.
placeholder: e.g. How fast is CO2 in the atmosphere rising?

source.name: DataHub
source.label: datahub.io
source.licence: public domain (ODC PDDL) and open licences as stated per dataset

examples: How fast is CO2 in the atmosphere rising?
Which countries have the biggest economies?
How much has the world warmed?
Which countries have the highest inflation?
How have oil prices changed since 2000?
How much have US house prices risen?
Is the sea level rising faster?
What is the US unemployment rate over time?
How much has gold gone up?
Where does the world's CO2 come from?
How much ice have glaciers lost?
How has the euro moved against the dollar?
Which US cities saw the biggest house price rises?
When was the stock market most volatile?
How have US interest rates changed?
Which countries have the most people?
How cheap is natural gas now?
